paper_sections.title: Conscious and unconscious brain responses to food and cocaine cues.
Main effect of time of day

description.value: The study assessed BOLD-fMRI responses to food, cocaine, and neutral visual cues presented subliminally or supraliminally, and examined whether cue reactivity differed between morning and evening sessions in healthy cocaine-naive volunteers.

design.value: Sixteen healthy volunteers completed an event-related food cue reactivity paradigm with three cue presentation times—33 ms, 750 ms, and 3000 ms—on two separate days, once between 9 and 11 AM and once between 5 and 7 PM, in randomized order. Each participant performed the three presentation-time sessions twice, with cue type and time of day treated as within-subject factors.

description.value: Participants rated “How negative/positive do you find the picture?” from -3 (very negative) to 3 (very positive) on a 7-point Likert scale.
Participants rated “How much does the picture excite you?” from 0 (not at all) to 6 (extremely) on a 7-point Likert scale.
Participants rated “How much do you want to consume the depicted item right now?” from 0 (not at all) to 6 (extremely) on a 7-point Likert scale.
Participants self-reported hunger levels before and after the scanning sessions on a 7-point Likert scale.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

description.value: The interview was used to assess the presence of drug abuse or dependence and neurological or psychiatric disorders, including eating disorders such as binge eating.

source_definition.value: The three cue categories were food, cocaine, and neutral.
Cues were presented for 33 ms, 750 ms, or 3000 ms; 33 ms was described as subliminal or unconscious and 750 and 3000 ms as supraliminal or conscious.
Participants were tested once in the morning between 9 and 11 AM and once in the evening between 5 and 7 PM.
The behavioral analyses included an interaction effect of cue type × time of day.

functional_form.value: a product of cue type and time of day

source_definition.value: Six realignment parameters were included as regressors of no interest.

description.value: Sixteen healthy individuals (6 females and 10 males) with an age range of 21 to 71 years old completed the study. Participants were naïve to cocaine use. Fourteen participants were included in further fMRI analyses after two participants had excessive head motion during MRI scans.

exclusion_criteria.value: neurological or psychiatric disorders, including eating disorders such as binge eating
excessive head motion during MRI scans (>2 mm)

diagnostic_system.value: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

clinical_characteristics.value: Body Mass Index ranged from 17.6 to 34.9 kg/m2 (mean=26.86±5.1SD).

medication_status.value: Participants were screened to exclude psychoactive medications.

task_description.value: A total of 40 appetitive food, 40 cocaine-related, and 40 neutral images were presented in a randomized order. Each participant performed three sessions with different cue presentation times—33 ms, 750 ms, and 3000 ms—and each task consisted of three runs showing 40 cues that included all three categories.

instructions.value: To ensure that participants were paying attention they were instructed to press a button if they saw an animal.

stimuli.value: Food pictures included appetitive high- and low-calorie foods, both savory and sweet, and both breakfast and dinner items, including bagels, sandwiches, ice cream and sorbet, salads, fruit salad, pizza, hamburgers, and pies. Cocaine pictures included bags of cocaine, lines of cocaine on a table, cocaine in spoons, cocaine pipes, and people smoking cocaine with faces cut off. Neutral pictures included neutral items from the International Affective Picture System and in-house picture libraries. Picture groups were matched for luminance.

task_performance_measures.value: button press if an animal was seen
self-reported hunger levels before and after scanning

instrument.value: 3 T Magnetom Prisma scanner (Siemens Medical Solutions USA, Inc., Malvern, PA)

description.value: A 32-channel head coil and a standard echo planar imaging sequence were used with sequential interleaved acquisition, 36 slices, and a slice thickness of 4 mm.

Functional data analysis was performed with SPM8. During preprocessing, scans were slice-time corrected, spatially realigned, co-registered to the T1 structural images, normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute template, and smoothed with a 6 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel.

software.value: SPM8 (Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK)

steps.value: co-registration to the T1 structural images
normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template
smoothing with a 6 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: For every participant and each session, three fMRI regressors—food, cocaine, and neutral events—were created and convolved with the hemodynamic response function with default temporal filtering of 128 s. Six realignment parameters were included as regressors of no interest. The single-subject contrasts were food>neutral, food>cocaine, and cocaine>neutral.

At the second level, a repeated measures factorial design included the first-level contrast images with presentation time (33, 750, and 3000 ms) and time of day (AM and PM) as within-subject factors. Whole-brain analyses used p<0.005 uncorrected at the voxel level, family-wise error corrected pFWE<0.05 at the cluster level, and a minimum cluster size of k>100; coordinates were reported in MNI space.
